# Independent audit: projective energy and maximal centroidal cap

Audited all six sections of
`candidate 49e262af8d182671`.
**PASS; no repair identified.** This is an independent proof audit. The
theorem is ordinary and supplies no cross-fiber or arithmetic conclusion.
The subsequently saved exact verifier was rerun: **12,004 checks PASS**
across 180 actual concave profiles, interval formulas and simplex cases.

## 1. Actual attainment and lower equality

The hinge integral is coercive because its restriction to a ball about
the prescribed source dominates the positive part of the linear form.
Differentiation uses a null cutting hyperplane at nonzero parameters,
while near zero the hinge is uniformly on its positive branch. The
minimizer's cap has a neighborhood of the source and hence positive
volume. Its stationarity is exactly the required zero first moment.

The inequality against every density `0<=f<=1` proves optimality of the
cap indicator directly. In the noncentroid case the cut is proper;
equality fixes the density on both sides almost everywhere. Two different
proper cut planes would change a positive-volume open region of the
body, so the cap and its normalized parameter are unique. The source
correctly does not assert parameter uniqueness in the centroid case.

The energy attainment argument matches the independently audited escort
proof and includes `d=1`. The positive-part tangent inequality in (10)
has the correct direction and is strict except at denominator one.
Its integral gives `E>=G(-(d+1)a)>=T`. A nonzero minimizing energy
parameter makes the first comparison strict on positive volume;
zero is minimizing exactly at the ordinary centroid. Thus the lower
equality classification is exact.

## 2. Matched cone profile and the negative extension

In the noncentroid case, the actual hinge cut coordinate has support
`[a,b]` with `a<0`, and the retained cap has mass `T` and coordinate
mean one. Homothety toward a highest cap point puts a copy of volume
`(1-t/b)^d T` above every height `t in [0,b]`; integrating its survival
function proves `b<=d+1`.

The cone density with coefficient `c=dT/(d+1)^d` has exactly the same
positive-half-line mass and first moment. Concavity of the actual
section root makes the positive difference interval connected. Unless
the two positive profiles agree almost everywhere, the zero mass and
first-moment differences force this interval to have endpoints strictly
between zero and `d+1`. The one-sign-change contradiction uses the
linear factor at the proposed endpoint and has the stated sign.

This reasoning does not require the profile difference to vanish
continuously at the actual body's top support: a jump there is harmless
for the sign-interval and secant arguments. Continuity at zero is
available because zero is an interior cutting level. The root difference
there is nonpositive, while it is positive somewhere above zero.
Concavity on the segment joining any negative level to that positive
point gives a strictly negative root difference at the negative level.
If the positive profiles agree, the same concavity calculation gives the
weak negative comparison instead.

The secant of an arbitrary finite convex kernel lies above that kernel
between the two sign-change endpoints and below it outside. Multiplying
by the negative/positive/negative profile difference therefore gives
the asserted integral order. The affine part cancels by BOTH matched
moments. No differentiability of sections or body-localization theorem
is assumed.

## 3. Strict upper bound, intervals and sharpness

The test energy parameter `-u*/(d+1)` has denominator
`(d+2-s)/(d+1)>=1/(d+1)` on the whole actual body. The positive convex
kernel comparison on `[0,d+1]`, together with the pointwise comparison
on negative levels, has the correct integrated direction. It is strict
because the finite body has no sections below its finite bottom level,
where the comparison cone remains positive. The cone integral is finite
and equals `T/(d+1)^d`; multiplying by the denominator scale proves
`E<(d+1)T`.

For an interval the formulas `T=2min(l,r)` and `E=4lr/(l+r)` give the
same strict upper constant directly. The simplex formula also checks:
the proposed vertex denominators interpolate one positive affine
denominator normalized at the marked point. Its projective image is a
simplex with centroid zero. Under the Jacobian this is exactly the
`L^(-d-2)` first-moment equation, so strict convexity certifies the
minimizer. The augmented-determinant operation gives the stated volume
factor `1/product L_i`.

For the approaching-vertex simplex family, the displayed hinge equals
one at the prescribed point, and its positive region is exactly the
homothetic simplex of centroid that point. Its zero moment certifies
the maximal retained mass, not merely a feasible subbody. The exact
ratio `(d+1)(1-d epsilon)` consequently proves sharpness of the
dimension constant and its nonattainment at interior marked points.

The retained subbody is an actual convex cap, but neither its law nor
its directional cap masses are identified with the escort measure.
The source explicitly retains this necessary limitation.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
